thesis_summary.thesis: Linde plc (LIN) is the world's largest industrial gases company, formed from the 2018 merger of Praxair and Linde AG. **[Fact]** It sells atmospheric and specialty gases through on-site plants (long take-or-pay contracts), merchant bulk delivery, and packaged cylinders to customers in manufacturing, healthcare, electronics, chemicals, and energy. **[Fact]** FY2025 sales were **$34.0 billion** (+3% versus FY2024), with four reportable segments: Americas, APAC, EMEA, and Linde Engineering. **[Fact]** CEO Sanjiv Lamba leads an Irish-domiciled company listed on Nasdaq; headquarters are in the United Kingdom and United States.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may treat Linde as a bond-proxy quality compounder and pay a premium multiple for oligopoly stability, underweighting that **$4.6 billion** of FY2025 share repurchases and rising long-term debt (**$20.7 billion** versus **$15.3 billion** prior year) compress future per-share growth if industrial volumes soften. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on adjusted earnings growth (+7% FY2025 diluted earnings per share) while the stock trades near **49 times** GAAP free cash flow per share at **$531.30**, leaving little margin of safety. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 sales rose **8%** and diluted earnings per share **13%**, so near-term fundamentals are strong; there is no dated predictive attribute, only a **descriptive** premium-multiple setup.

Global gases oligopoly; on-site pricing and electronics/hydrogen demand; buybacks ~2% annual share reduction

Hydrogen and electronics project pipeline: incremental return on invested capital evidence
Mechanical refresh price **$531.30** (Yahoo 2026-07-10); stance remains watch below 15% hurdle
